title: Read the 1 star reviews of your favorite games to understand how little the negativity matters
author: TheUniverseOrNothing
selftext:
Very important that you can know the difference between valid criticism or simply somebody that you cannot make happy. 

Especially in the world of AI we are going to be scrutinized under a microscope.

But for example take my favorite movie of all time, interstellar, and then go read the 1 star negative reviews. The movie was highly successful and personally my favorite. I can watch it every year and never get tired of it. Same applies to all the games we love.

The 1 star reviews are not your target audience. I probably couldn’t be friends with these people or enjoy dinner conversations with them. Not because they have to like the movie, that’s completely acceptable. But when you read how these people review things and complain about everything… you just have to accept you are not going to please everyone. And some people are miserable. I mean seriously in no world does this movie merit 1 star even if you hate it.

It’s posted here everyday and most people with common sense understand this most basic principle. You make a fun game that people enjoy and they will come. It does not matter how you get to that point.

If you’ve made a worthy game you will see the support. Even though the AI game dev attracts the most miserable people, if your post shows that people genuinely enjoy your project, stay focused and keep building.

Once your game hits 1 million in sales and you are highly successful, there is still going to be endless Reddit posts about how it was AI slop and a horrible game.

You literally cannot win if you don’t learn how to distinguish your average gamer from a chronically online anti-ai purist. 

I love OSRS and used to be made fun of in school for playing it. Well guess what, 15 years later I still love the game and jagex is rolling in money. Same thing applies to building game, I’m going to build what I think is fun and if you want to be a bully over it you simply do not matter. Like an annoying mosquito buzzing in the ear that needs to be swatted away and we move on with life.

comments.author: Valdaraak
comments.body: General rule is to ignore 1 star and 5 star reviews. 2-4 are where you actually get value.
